title: Why Does Your Foot Fall Asleep?
description:
Why does your foot fall asleep? It isn't really asleep: when you sit on your foot or cross your legs, you squash a nerve and the tiny blood vessels that feed it. A squashed nerve can't pass messages, so your brain stops hearing from your foot and it goes numb. When you stand up, the pressure lifts and the nerve restarts all at once, firing messy signals. That buzzing static is the pins and needles feeling.

A short, occasional dead foot is normal and fades within a minute or so. If tingling keeps coming back with no obvious cause, talk to a doctor.

Where does your foot usually fall asleep? Tell us below.
